option_description: Whether the inter-broker / replication (east-west) channel carries traffic over TLS rather than cleartext (Kafka security.inter.broker.protocol=SSL/SASL_SSL; MSK EncryptionInTransit.InCluster=true; Pulsar replicationTlsEnabled+brokerClientTlsEnabled; RabbitMQ -proto_dist inet_tls; NATS cluster/gateway tls{}; Redis tls-replication/tls-cluster).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Cleartext inter-broker / replication channel" — fires (is_false) when the replication listener speaks PLAINTEXT / InCluster=false / inet_tcp default / no route TLS, exposing replicated payloads and SASL credentials to on-path sniffing (T1040).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Kafka inter-broker protocol and listener-to-protocol mapping.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: security.inter.broker.protocol=SSL or SASL_SSL (secure); the listener named by inter.broker.listener.name must map to SSL/SASL_SSL in listener.security.protocol.map. PLAINTEXT (or default) = insecure cleartext inter-broker.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect Pulsar geo-replication TLS flags.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: replicationTlsEnabled=true and brokerClientTlsEnabled=true (Pulsar geo-replication encrypted). Absent/false = replicator traffic in cleartext.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Probe the inter-broker port for a live TLS handshake on the wire.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A completed TLS handshake (Protocol TLSv1.2/1.3, a real cipher) on the inter-broker port = encrypted. Connection refused-as-plaintext / no handshake = cleartext replication listener.

option_description: Whether the inter-broker / replication join path enforces mutual TLS, requiring each peer to present a CA-signed broker identity before joining replication (Kafka ssl.client.auth=required on the inter-broker listener; RabbitMQ inter_node_tls verify_peer+fail_if_no_peer_cert; NATS cluster/gateway tls verify_and_map).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Rogue broker / unauthenticated cluster join" — fires (is_false) when peer certs are not enforced (none/requested/verify_none), letting a rogue node join as a peer and read/forge replicated partitions (T1078).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm Kafka enforces client-cert auth on the inter-broker listener and the inter-broker principal is a super.user.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ssl.client.auth=required; the inter-broker principal (cert CN) listed in super.users. none/requested = inter-broker peers not cryptographically authenticated.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm RabbitMQ inter-node TLS verifies peer certs.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: server section: {verify, verify_peer} and {fail_if_no_peer_cert, true} = mTLS between nodes. verify_none / fail_if_no_peer_cert false = peers not authenticated.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm NATS cluster routes require a verified mapped peer cert.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: cluster{} contains a tls{} map with cert_file/ca_file and verify (or verify_and_map). No tls{} under cluster{} = unencrypted/unauthenticated routes.

option_description: Whether the cluster permits anonymous/unauthenticated peers to join or act (MSK ClientAuthentication.Unauthenticated.Enabled=true, or allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found=true; any broker accepting cluster membership without proving identity).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Rogue broker / unauthenticated cluster join" — fires (is_true) when an unauthenticated node can become a cluster peer / replication participant (T1078).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the MSK cluster's client-authentication posture.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Sasl/Tls enabled and Unauthenticated.Enabled=false. Unauthenticated true = anonymous access permitted.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the Kafka broker does not allow everyone when no ACL is found.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found=false with an authorizer configured. true = anonymous/unauthorized peers effectively permitted.

option_description: Whether server-to-server cluster routes / gateway connections require route-level authorization (credential or mapped identity) before joining the mesh, independent of transport encryption (NATS cluster{authorization{}} and gateway{authorization{}}; Pulsar/Kafka inter-broker principal in super.users/ACLs).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Rogue broker / unauthenticated cluster join" — fires (is_false) when discovered routes accept unauthorized peers, allowing an attacker server to route into the cluster (T1078).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm NATS cluster routes require user/password authorization.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: authorization{} with user/password present under cluster{}. Absent = routes accept unauthenticated peers.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the Kafka inter-broker principal is explicitly authorized (super.users / ACLs).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The inter-broker cert CN appears in super.users (or has explicit ClusterAction ACLs). Missing = routes/peers not authorized at the cluster layer.

option_description: Whether geo-replication / cross-cluster brokers authenticate to remote peers using a broker-client auth plugin (Pulsar brokerClientTlsEnabled + brokerClientAuthenticationPlugin=AuthenticationTls with brokerClientTrustCertsFilePath; Kafka MM2 per-cluster SSL keystore identity).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Rogue broker / unauthenticated cluster join" — fires (is_false) when replication connects to peer clusters anonymously, letting an unverified/spoofed broker participate in replication (T1078).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm Pulsar broker-client auth plugin is set for replication.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: brokerClientTlsEnabled=true with a non-empty brokerClientAuthenticationPlugin and trust certs path. Empty plugin = unauthenticated broker-to-broker replication.
how_to_obtain.source: Apache Pulsar geo-replication / TLS authentication docs

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the registered remote cluster uses TLS-secure service URLs and an auth plugin.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Remote cluster registered with the TLS (secure) service URLs (--broker-url-secure / --url-secure) and an auth plugin, not the plaintext URLs.

option_description: Whether the shared secret gating RabbitMQ cluster membership (the Erlang cookie / .erlang.cookie) is a long, high-entropy, randomly-generated value distributed out-of-band — not a default, predictable, or weak value. Any process presenting the same cookie can join the Erlang distribution and run rabbitmqctl.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Weak/default Erlang cookie enabling rogue RabbitMQ node" (and also referenced by "Replication credential / Erlang-cookie exposure at rest") — fires (is_false) when the cookie is default/predictable/weak so a rogue node can join (T1552).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the .erlang.cookie file permissions, owner, and value entropy.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Permissions 400 (or 600) owned by rabbitmq; file content high-entropy. World/group-readable or default value = rogue-node cluster-join risk.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the cookie was generated randomly and distributed out-of-band rather than shipped with the package or copied from documentation/examples.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Operator confirms the cookie is a per-cluster random secret from a generator/secret store, not a default, hostname-derived, or reused/example value.

option_description: Whether the on-disk cluster-membership secret file (.erlang.cookie) is protected with restrictive ownership and permissions — mode 0400 (or 0600) owned by the rabbitmq service user, not world- or group-readable.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Weak/default Erlang cookie enabling rogue RabbitMQ node" (and also "Replication credential / Erlang-cookie exposure at rest") — fires (is_false) when world/group-readable, letting any local process read the standing credential and take over the cluster (T1552).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the mode and owner of the .erlang.cookie file.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Permissions 400 (or 600) owned by rabbitmq; file content high-entropy. World/group-readable or default value = rogue-node cluster-join risk.

option_description: Whether the replication/mirror principal (Kafka MirrorMaker/MM2 user, RabbitMQ federation/shovel user, NATS account, Pulsar broker-client identity) is scoped to only the operations replication needs — source READ + target WRITE/ClusterAction/IdempotentWrite on the specific mirrored resources — with no cluster-wide ALL/admin grant.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Over-broad replication / mirror credentials" — fires (is_false) when the mirror principal holds broad Allow ALL / Topic:* / cluster admin, so a compromised mirror process can read/write arbitrary topics/queues across both clusters (T1078).

how_to_obtain.instruction: List the Kafka ACLs bound to the mirror principal.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only the narrow ACLs replication needs (Read on source topics, Write/ClusterAction/IdempotentWrite on target). Allow ALL / Topic:* / cluster admin = over-broad replication creds.

how_to_obtain.instruction: List the RabbitMQ federation/shovel user's permissions.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Federation/shovel user limited to the specific vhost + resources it mirrors; '.*' configure/write/read on all vhosts = over-broad.

option_description: Whether the replication/mirror credential is a dedicated identity used solely for the replication path, not shared with application/client principals.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Over-broad replication / mirror credentials" — fires (is_false) when replication reuses an application or shared-admin principal, collapsing the blast radius so a compromise grants both application access and cross-cluster replication read/write (T1078).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Identify the principal used by the mirror/federation path and confirm it is distinct from app/client principals (compare its CN/username against application ACL subjects).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The replication principal is a distinct identity not also used by application clients. Same principal appearing on application ACLs = shared credential reuse.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm with operators that the federation/shovel/MM2 credential is provisioned exclusively for replication and not reused as an app or admin login.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A dedicated replication identity is documented; no application or shared-admin credential is reused for the replication path.

option_description: Whether the set of remote clusters permitted to participate in federation/geo-replication is explicitly enumerated (Kafka MM2 source/target list, Pulsar clusters list, NATS gateways[], RabbitMQ federation upstreams) and matches the intended topology.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Untrusted / spoofed federation or geo-replication peer" — fires (is_false) on wildcard / unbounded peer acceptance, letting an untrusted or attacker-impersonated cluster cross the trust boundary and inject/exfiltrate replicated messages (T1199).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate the registered Pulsar peer clusters and inspect each.
how_to_obtain.command: pulsar-admin clusters list && for c in $(pulsar-admin clusters list); do pulsar-admin clusters get $c; done
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only intended peer clusters are registered, each with TLS-secure URLs. Unexpected cluster entries = untrusted federation peer.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Architecture review of the registered peer set against the intended federation topology.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Architecture review: the set of registered remote clusters (Kafka MM2 source/target list, Pulsar clusters list, NATS gateways[], RabbitMQ federation upstreams) matches the intended federation topology; truststore/CA scope does not trust beyond the federation.

option_description: Whether the trust store backing inter-cluster federation/geo-replication is limited to the federation CA(s) only, not a public/wide CA bundle.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Untrusted / spoofed federation or geo-replication peer" — fires (is_false) on over-broad CA trust, where any cluster bearing a certificate from the broadly-trusted CA can impersonate a legitimate federation peer (T1199).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the federation truststore / CA scope against the federation boundary.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Architecture review: truststore/CA scope does not trust beyond the federation — it contains only the federation CA(s), not a public/wide CA bundle.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Pulsar broker-client trust certs path used for replication and confirm it points at the federation CA bundle, not the system/public trust store.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: brokerClientTrustCertsFilePath references a dedicated federation CA file. A public/system CA bundle here = over-broad CA trust.
how_to_obtain.source: Apache Pulsar geo-replication / TLS authentication docs

option_description: Whether each registered remote federation/replication endpoint is verified (TLS-secure service URLs, peer identity bound to the expected named cluster) rather than accepted unverified.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Untrusted / spoofed federation or geo-replication peer" — fires (is_false) on unverified remote cluster endpoints, where a spoofed endpoint can substitute for a legitimate peer (T1199).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm each registered remote cluster uses TLS-secure URLs and is bound to the expected named cluster.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Remote cluster registered with the TLS (secure) service URLs (--broker-url-secure / --url-secure) and an auth plugin, not the plaintext URLs.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Handshake against the registered remote endpoint and verify the served cert CN/SAN matches the expected named peer cluster.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Served certificate subject/issuer matches the expected named peer cluster and federation CA. Mismatch / self-signed / unexpected CN = unverified or spoofed endpoint.

option_description: Whether replication/federation endpoint credentials are embedded inline in connection URIs at rest (e.g. RabbitMQ federation/shovel amqps://user:pass@host URIs).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Replication credential / Erlang-cookie exposure at rest" — fires (is_true) when standing creds sit in plaintext config and can be read to impersonate the replication path (T1552).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect RabbitMQ federation/shovel/upstream definitions for inline user:pass@host credentials in the URIs.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Upstream/shovel URIs reference credentials indirectly or via a vault; an amqps://user:pass@host with a literal password = credentials embedded in URI at rest.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep on-disk federation/shovel definition files for embedded credentials in amqp(s) URIs.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No matches = creds not inlined. Any amqps://user:pass@host hit = replication credentials embedded in URI at rest.

option_description: Whether replication credentials (MirrorMaker keystore/truststore passwords, federation/shovel passwords, broker-client auth parameters) are externalized out of plaintext config files rather than written literally into them.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Replication credential / Erlang-cookie exposure at rest" — fires (is_false) when creds sit in cleartext config at rest, readable to impersonate the replication path (T1552).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect MirrorMaker/Connect and broker config for literal keystore/truststore passwords vs indirect references.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Passwords resolved via ${env}/secret refs or a config provider, not literal cleartext values. A literal password string = credentials in cleartext config at rest.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm replication credentials are injected at runtime (env/secret ref/config provider) rather than committed to the config file.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Operators confirm an indirection mechanism (Kafka ConfigProvider, env interpolation, secret mount) supplies the credential; nothing literal in the checked-in config.

option_description: Whether replication credentials and keystore passwords are sourced from a managed secret store / secret manager rather than committed to disk in cleartext.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Replication credential / Erlang-cookie exposure at rest" — fires (is_false) when secrets are stored on disk rather than resolved from a managed store at runtime (T1552).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm replication credentials/keystore passwords are resolved from a managed secret store (Vault, AWS/GCP secret manager, K8s secrets via CSI) at runtime.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A managed secret store is the source of record for replication creds; values are injected at start/runtime rather than written to disk in cleartext.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check that config references secret-manager paths/refs rather than literal secret values.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Config carries secret-store references/placeholders, not inline secret material. Literal secrets on disk = not resolved via a secret manager.

option_description: Whether the on-disk replication config files holding credentials (broker.conf, server.properties, MirrorMaker/connect properties, federation definitions) have restrictive ownership/permissions and are not world/group-readable.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Replication credential / Erlang-cookie exposure at rest" — fires (is_false) when the config files are world/group-readable, exposing any embedded replication credentials (T1552).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the mode and owner of the replication config files that may hold credentials.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Mode 0600/0640 owned by the broker service user, not world/group-readable (no trailing rwx for other). World/group-readable = config secrets exposed at rest.

option_description: Whether the inter-broker/replication listener is bound to a private/internal interface and firewalled so it is reachable only from peer cluster nodes (a dedicated INTERNAL listener on a private interface; the inter-broker port filtered/closed from the client/public network).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Inter-broker listener not network-isolated" — fires (is_false) when the replication port is bound broadly (0.0.0.0) or reachable from client/public networks, exposing the east-west channel to rogue-join and on-path sniffing even with TLS on (T1040).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm Kafka uses a distinct internal listener bound to a private interface for inter-broker traffic.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A distinct INTERNAL listener bound to the private interface is used for inter.broker.listener.name, separate from the client listener. Single 0.0.0.0 listener shared with clients = no isolation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Scan the inter-broker port from a client/public network position.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Inter-broker port filtered/closed from client/public networks; open from anywhere = exposed replication listener.

option_description: Whether the inter-broker/replication port is reachable from a public/internet-facing or client network position (advertised/bound on 0.0.0.0, no firewall/security-group restriction to the peer subnet).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Inter-broker listener not network-isolated" — fires (is_true) when the replication port is reachable from outside the cluster trust zone, inviting rogue broker join and traffic capture (T1040).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Scan the replication port from outside the cluster trust zone (public/internet position).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Inter-broker port filtered/closed from client/public networks; open from anywhere = exposed replication listener.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the firewall/security-group rules guarding the replication port.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Security-group/firewall scopes the inter-broker port to the peer subnet only. A 0.0.0.0/0 or client-network allow rule = internet/client-reachable replication listener.

option_description: Whether the inter-broker/replication channel uses a distinct listener/interface dedicated to peer-node traffic, separate from the client-facing listener (e.g. inter.broker.listener.name points at a distinct INTERNAL listener, not the shared client listener).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Inter-broker listener not network-isolated" — fires (is_false) when a single shared listener serves both clients and replication, removing the segmentation that would let the replication port be firewalled independently to peers only (T1040).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm inter.broker.listener.name points at a dedicated INTERNAL listener distinct from the client listener.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A distinct INTERNAL listener bound to the private interface is used for inter.broker.listener.name, separate from the client listener. Single 0.0.0.0 listener shared with clients = no isolation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify the inter-broker port differs from / is reachable separately to the client port.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Distinct ports/interfaces for replication vs clients, allowing independent firewalling. Same single port serving both = shared listener, no segmentation.
